title: Luke Chapter 21 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Luke chapter 21 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Luke Chapter 21 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Luke Chapter 21.

questions.question: In Luke 21, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The poor widow casting two mites into the treasury
Jesus predicting that not one stone of the temple will be left upon another
Jesus seeing rich men casting their gifts into the treasury
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus seeing rich men casting their gifts into the treasury
questions.explanation: Luke 21:1 states that Jesus looked up and saw the rich men casting their gifts into the treasury, which is the first event mentioned in the chapter.

questions.question: What did the poor widow cast into the treasury?
questions.correctAnswer: Two mites
questions.explanation: Luke 21:2 clearly states that the poor widow cast in two mites.

questions.question: According to Jesus, who has cast in more than all others?
questions.correctAnswer: The poor widow
questions.explanation: Luke 21:3 states that Jesus said the poor widow has cast in more than all others.

questions.question: Why did Jesus say the poor widow gave more than the rich men?
options: She gave all the living she had
questions.correctAnswer: She gave all the living she had
questions.explanation: Luke 21:4 explains that the widow gave all the living that she had, unlike the rich who gave from their abundance.

questions.question: What did some people speak about concerning the temple?
options: How it was adorned with goodly stones and gifts
questions.correctAnswer: How it was adorned with goodly stones and gifts
questions.explanation: Luke 21:5 records that some spoke about the temple’s adornment with goodly stones and gifts.

questions.question: What did Jesus say would happen to the stones of the temple?
options: Not one stone will be left upon another
They would be moved to another place
questions.correctAnswer: Not one stone will be left upon another
questions.explanation: Luke 21:6 clearly states that days will come when not one stone will be left upon another.

questions.question: What question did the people ask Jesus after hearing about the temple's destruction?
options: When shall these things be and what sign will there be?
Who will build the new temple?
questions.correctAnswer: When shall these things be and what sign will there be?
questions.explanation: Luke 21:7 shows they asked Jesus when these things would happen and what signs would indicate their coming.

questions.question: What warning did Jesus give about false Christs?
options: They will be accepted by all
They will come after the destruction
questions.correctAnswer: Do not follow them
questions.explanation: Luke 21:8 warns to take heed and not to follow those who say 'I am Christ.'

questions.question: What should people do when they hear of wars and commotions, according to Jesus?
questions.correctAnswer: Do not be terrified
questions.explanation: Luke 21:9 instructs not to be terrified when hearing about wars and commotions.

questions.question: According to Jesus, who will rise against whom?
options: Nation shall rise against nation and kingdom against kingdom
questions.correctAnswer: Nation shall rise against nation and kingdom against kingdom
questions.explanation: Luke 21:10 states that nation shall rise against nation and kingdom against kingdom.

questions.question: Which of the following signs did Jesus mention would occur in divers places?
questions.correctAnswer: Great earthquakes
questions.explanation: Luke 21:11 mentions great earthquakes in divers places as one of the signs.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus said that before all these signs, believers will be persecuted and brought before rulers for His name's sake.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Luke 21:12 states that before these signs, believers will be persecuted and brought before kings and rulers for Jesus’ name’s sake.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus said that persecution will turn to you for a testimony.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Luke 21:13 says that persecution will turn to you for a testimony.

questions.question: True or False: The text says that the poor widow gave two silver coins.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Luke 21:2 specifies that the poor widow gave two mites, not two silver coins.

questions.question: True or False: The chapter states that the end will come immediately after wars and commotions.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Luke 21:9 clarifies that although wars and commotions will happen, the end is not immediately after.

medium.title: Luke Chapter 21 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Luke Chapter 21 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What must you not meditate on before you answer when brought before others?
questions.correctAnswer: What you shall answer
questions.explanation: This is based on Luke 21:14, which instructs not to meditate before what you shall answer.

questions.question: What does Luke 21:15 promise will happen if someone does not meditate on their answer before speaking?
questions.correctAnswer: They will be given wisdom
questions.explanation: Luke 21:15 states that God will give you a mouth and wisdom, which implies that relying on Him leads to wise answers.

questions.question: Who does Luke 21:16 say will betray you?
options: Your parents, brethren, kinsfolks, and friends
questions.correctAnswer: Your parents, brethren, kinsfolks, and friends
questions.explanation: Luke 21:16 specifically mentions that betrayal will come from family and friends.

questions.question: What should those in Judaea do when they see armies surrounding Jerusalem according to Luke 21:21?
questions.correctAnswer: Flee to the mountains
questions.explanation: Luke 21:21 instructs those in Judaea to flee to the mountains when they see Jerusalem compassed with armies.

questions.question: What does Luke 21:18 say about the safety of the faithful?
options: They will not lose their lives
questions.correctAnswer: They will not lose their lives
questions.explanation: Verse Luke 21:18 reassures that not a hair of your head will perish, indicating divine protection.

questions.question: According to Luke 21:23, what will happen to those with children during the days of distress?
questions.correctAnswer: Woe unto them
questions.explanation: Luke 21:23 expresses woe for those with children during the coming distress, highlighting the challenges they will face.

questions.question: What does Luke 21:19 encourage the faithful to do?
questions.correctAnswer: Possess their souls in patience
questions.explanation: Luke 21:19 encourages believers to maintain their composure and patience during trials.

questions.question: What is said to happen to Jerusalem according to Luke 21:24?
options: It will be a place of peace
It shall be trodden down of the Gentiles
questions.correctAnswer: It shall be trodden down of the Gentiles
questions.explanation: Luke 21:24 states that Jerusalem will be trodden down by the Gentiles until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.

questions.question: What signs will there be in the heavens according to Luke 21:25?
options: Signs in the sun, moon, and stars
questions.correctAnswer: Signs in the sun, moon, and stars
questions.explanation: Luke 21:25 mentions signs in the sun, moon, and stars as part of the prophetic signs to come.

questions.question: What will happen to men's hearts according to Luke 21:26?
options: They will be filled with joy
They will be failing for fear
questions.correctAnswer: They will be failing for fear
questions.explanation: Luke 21:26 describes a time when men's hearts will fail them for fear of what is coming upon the earth.

questions.question: What does Luke 21:20 indicate is near when armies surround Jerusalem?
questions.correctAnswer: Desolation
questions.explanation: Luke 21:20 states that when armies surround Jerusalem, the desolation thereof is near.

questions.question: According to Luke 21:12, what will believers face before the end times?
questions.correctAnswer: Persecution
questions.explanation: Luke 21:12 mentions that believers will be delivered up for persecution before the end times.

questions.question: True or False: In Luke 21:15, Jesus promises that adversaries will be unable to resist the wisdom given to believers.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Luke 21:15 states that God will provide believers with wisdom that adversaries cannot resist.

questions.question: True or False: According to Luke 21:4, the rich contribute more to the offerings than the poor.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Luke 21:4 indicates that the poor widow gave more than all the rich, highlighting the value of sacrificial giving.

questions.question: True or False: Luke 21:8 warns believers against being deceived by those claiming to be Christ.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Luke 21:8 indeed warns not to be deceived by false claims of Christ, as many will come in His name.

hard.title: Luke Chapter 21 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Luke Chapter 21.

questions.question: According to Luke 21:27, how will the Son of Man be seen when He comes?
options: coming in a cloud with power and great glory
riding on a white horse with a sword
appearing in the temple with a loud voice
questions.correctAnswer: coming in a cloud with power and great glory
questions.explanation: Luke 21:27 states, 'And then shall they see the Son of man coming in a cloud with power and great glory,' indicating the manner of His coming.

questions.question: What does Jesus instruct believers to do when these signs begin to happen, according to Luke 21:28?
options: look up, and lift up your heads; for your redemption draweth nigh
hide in the mountains until the danger passes
gather together in the temple to pray
questions.correctAnswer: look up, and lift up your heads; for your redemption draweth nigh
questions.explanation: Luke 21:28 directs believers to 'look up, and lift up your heads; for your redemption draweth nigh' when these things begin to come to pass.

questions.question: In the parable Jesus speaks in Luke 21:29-30, what does the fig tree shooting forth its leaves signify?
options: that summer is now nigh at hand
the coming of a great famine
questions.correctAnswer: that summer is now nigh at hand
questions.explanation: Luke 21:30 explains that when the fig tree and all the trees shoot forth leaves, 'ye see and know of your own selves that summer is now nigh at hand.'

questions.question: What assurance does Jesus give about the fulfillment of the prophesied events in Luke 21:32?
options: This generation shall not pass away, till all be fulfilled
Only after many generations will these things be fulfilled
These things will never be fulfilled
The fulfillment is delayed until the end of the age
questions.correctAnswer: This generation shall not pass away, till all be fulfilled
questions.explanation: Luke 21:32 states, 'Verily I say unto you, This generation shall not pass away, till all be fulfilled,' assuring that the events will occur within that generation.

questions.question: According to Luke 21:33, how do the permanence of heaven and earth compare to Jesus' words?
options: Heaven and earth shall pass away: but my words shall not pass away
Heaven and earth shall endure forever, as shall my words
My words will fade, but heaven and earth will remain
Both heaven, earth, and my words are temporary
questions.correctAnswer: Heaven and earth shall pass away: but my words shall not pass away
questions.explanation: Luke 21:33 contrasts the temporary nature of heaven and earth with the eternal nature of Jesus' words, saying, 'Heaven and earth shall pass away: but my words shall not pass away.'

questions.question: What is the exhortation given in Luke 21:36 to believers in light of the coming events?
options: Watch ye therefore, and pray always, that ye may be accounted worthy to escape all these things
Flee to the mountains immediately and do not look back
Build strongholds to protect yourselves from the coming woes
Preach loudly to all nations to repent before it is too late
questions.correctAnswer: Watch ye therefore, and pray always, that ye may be accounted worthy to escape all these things
questions.explanation: Luke 21:36 instructs believers to 'Watch ye therefore, and pray always, that ye may be accounted worthy to escape all these things that shall come to pass, and to stand before the Son of man.'

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'ἐπερχομένων' (eperchomenon) in Luke 21:28 mean?
questions.correctAnswer: begin to come to pass
questions.explanation: In Luke 21:28, the Greek word 'ἐπερχομένων' is translated as 'begin to come to pass,' indicating the onset of the prophesied events.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Luke 21:29-31 with the parable of the fig tree?
questions.correctAnswer: Typology
questions.explanation: Luke 21:29-31 uses typology, where the fig tree’s budding represents the nearness of the kingdom of God, a symbolic foreshadowing of future events.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage connects to the theme of the Son of Man coming with power and glory as described in Luke 21:27?
questions.correctAnswer: Daniel 7:13-14
questions.explanation: Daniel 7:13-14 describes 'one like a son of man' coming with clouds of heaven and receiving dominion and glory, connecting directly with Luke 21:27.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the warning in Luke 21:34 about hearts being overcharged with surfeiting and drunkenness?
questions.correctAnswer: 1 Thessalonians 5:6-8
questions.explanation: 1 Thessalonians 5:6-8 warns believers to stay sober and vigilant, echoing the caution in Luke 21:34 against being overcharged with surfeiting and drunkenness.

questions.question: What immediately precedes the description of the Son of Man coming in a cloud in Luke 21:27?
options: Men's hearts failing them for fear and looking after those things coming on the earth
The parable of the fig tree
questions.correctAnswer: Men's hearts failing them for fear and looking after those things coming on the earth
questions.explanation: Luke 21:26, immediately before verse 27, describes 'Men's hearts failing them for fear, and for looking after those things which are coming on the earth,' setting the context for the Son of Man's coming.

questions.question: How does the passage Luke 21:34-35 function as a literary device in relation to the theme of vigilance?
options: It uses inclusio by framing the warning to watch with a call to prayer
It uses allegory to describe spiritual blindness
It uses irony in describing the day as a snare
It uses parallelism between drunkenness and surfeiting
questions.correctAnswer: It uses inclusio by framing the warning to watch with a call to prayer
questions.explanation: Luke 21:34-36 uses inclusio by warning against being overcharged and then commanding watchfulness and prayer, framing vigilance thematically.

questions.question: From a historical context, what is the significance of Jesus teaching in the temple by day and lodging on the Mount of Olives by night as stated in Luke 21:37?
options: It reflects the traditional Jewish practice of teaching in the temple and retreating to the mount for solitude
It indicates Jesus was avoiding Roman authorities by staying outside the city at night
It shows Jesus’ rejection of the temple as a holy place
It was a symbol of Jesus’ royal status over Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: It reflects the traditional Jewish practice of teaching in the temple and retreating to the mount for solitude
questions.explanation: Luke 21:37 shows Jesus' pattern of teaching publicly in the temple and withdrawing to the Mount of Olives, a known place of prayer and solitude consistent with Jewish customs.

questions.question: According to Luke 21:32, what interpretive challenge does the phrase 'This generation shall not pass away' present to scholars?
options: Determining whether 'generation' refers to Jesus’ contemporaries or a symbolic age
Whether 'generation' means the entire human race
If 'generation' means only the Jewish people or all nations
Whether 'generation' indicates a future millennial kingdom
questions.correctAnswer: Determining whether 'generation' refers to Jesus’ contemporaries or a symbolic age
questions.explanation: Luke 21:32 raises interpretive questions about the meaning of 'generation,' whether it is literal (Jesus' contemporaries) or figurative (an age), affecting eschatological understanding.

questions.question: True or False: Luke 21:38 indicates that people came early in the morning to the temple specifically to hear Jesus teach.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Luke 21:38 states, 'And all the people came early in the morning to him in the temple, for to hear him,' confirming that people came early to listen to Jesus.

theological.title: Luke Chapter 21 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Luke Chapter 21 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Luke 21:4 teach about the nature of true sacrifice in salvation?
options: True sacrifice is measured by the amount given.
True sacrifice is the giving of all one has, especially in poverty.
True sacrifice is only valid if given by the wealthy.
questions.correctAnswer: True sacrifice is the giving of all one has, especially in poverty.
questions.explanation: Luke 21:4 highlights that the poor widow cast in 'all the living that she had,' teaching that true sacrifice is not the quantity but the heart and totality of giving in faith.

questions.question: What doctrine about eschatological deception is taught in Luke 21:8?
options: Christians should follow all who claim to be the Christ.
Many false Christs will come, so believers must be vigilant against deception.
Deception is impossible in the last days.
Only one false Christ will appear at the end.
questions.correctAnswer: Many false Christs will come, so believers must be vigilant against deception.
questions.explanation: Luke 21:8 warns believers to 'take heed that ye be not deceived' because 'many shall come in my name, saying, I am Christ,' emphasizing the doctrine of spiritual vigilance against false messiahs.

questions.question: What doctrine regarding divine providence over persecution is taught in Luke 21:18?
options: Believers will be physically harmed without exception.
God protects the ultimate welfare of believers even amidst persecution.
Believers will be miraculously delivered from every trial.
questions.correctAnswer: God protects the ultimate welfare of believers even amidst persecution.
questions.explanation: Luke 21:18 states 'there shall not an hair of your head perish,' teaching that God's providential care preserves believers ultimately despite physical threats.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Luke 21:33 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Immutability
questions.explanation: Luke 21:33 states 'my words shall not pass away,' demonstrating God's immutability, the unchanging and enduring nature of His word and promises.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is exemplified by God's promise in Luke 21:15 to give wisdom and speech to believers?
questions.correctAnswer: Providence
questions.explanation: Luke 21:15 shows God's providence in providing believers with 'a mouth and wisdom,' indicating His active care and guidance in their trials.

questions.question: How does Luke 21:20-24 connect to the broader biblical narrative of God's judgment and restoration of Jerusalem?
options: It anticipates the complete destruction of Jerusalem with no future hope.
It depicts Jerusalem's siege as a fulfillment of prophetic judgment leading to eventual restoration.
It denies any historical judgment upon Jerusalem.
It claims Jerusalem will be abandoned permanently.
questions.correctAnswer: It depicts Jerusalem's siege as a fulfillment of prophetic judgment leading to eventual restoration.
questions.explanation: Luke 21:20-24 describes Jerusalem's desolation and Gentile domination 'until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled,' linking to prophetic cycles of judgment and eventual restoration in Scripture.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical theme is prepared for in Luke 21:27 concerning the Son of man's coming?
options: The final judgment and consummation of the kingdom of God.
The establishment of an earthly political kingdom.
The end of the Jewish covenant.
The rejection of the Messiah by all nations.
questions.correctAnswer: The final judgment and consummation of the kingdom of God.
questions.explanation: Luke 21:27's depiction of the Son of man coming 'in a cloud with power and great glory' anticipates the eschatological return and final establishment of God's kingdom as taught throughout Scripture.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses Luke 21:12 and Luke 21:15 teach about divine empowerment amid persecution?
options: Believers face persecution without any divine support.
God empowers believers with wisdom and speech to witness despite persecution.
Persecution should be avoided at all costs.
questions.correctAnswer: God empowers believers with wisdom and speech to witness despite persecution.
questions.explanation: Luke 21:12 warns of persecution, and Luke 21:15 promises God will give 'a mouth and wisdom' so believers can testify effectively, teaching God's empowering presence in suffering.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Luke 21:25 and Luke 21:26 teach about cosmic signs and human response in eschatology?
options: Cosmic signs are irrelevant to human fear and faith.
Cosmic disturbances will cause widespread fear and perplexity as part of the end-times scenario.
Cosmic signs are merely natural phenomena with no theological significance.
Humans will remain calm and unaffected by cosmic events.
questions.correctAnswer: Cosmic disturbances will cause widespread fear and perplexity as part of the end-times scenario.
questions.explanation: Luke 21:25-26 describe signs in sun, moon, stars, and distress of nations causing 'men's hearts failing them for fear,' illustrating the theological reality of cosmic upheaval inducing human terror at the end.

questions.question: What doctrine about watchfulness and prayer is taught by combining Luke 21:34 and Luke 21:36?
options: Believers can ignore watchfulness and still be ready.
Watchfulness and constant prayer are necessary to avoid being overtaken by unexpected eschatological judgment.
Surfeiting and drunkenness help spiritual alertness.
Prayer alone without watchfulness is sufficient.
questions.correctAnswer: Watchfulness and constant prayer are necessary to avoid being overtaken by unexpected eschatological judgment.
questions.explanation: Luke 21:34 warns against being overcharged by life's cares, and 21:36 commands to 'watch ye therefore, and pray always' to be accounted worthy to escape, teaching the vital role of vigilance and prayer.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Luke 21:7-11 only predicts vague social unrest and natural disasters with no real eschatological significance. What does Luke 21:7-11 actually teach?
options: It predicts specific signs that precede the end times, including wars, earthquakes, famines, and heavenly signs.
It only discusses general societal problems unrelated to eschatology.
It suggests that the end will come without any signs.
questions.correctAnswer: It predicts specific signs that precede the end times, including wars, earthquakes, famines, and heavenly signs.
questions.explanation: Luke 21:7-11 provides a detailed list of apocalyptic signs like 'nation against nation,' 'earthquakes,' and 'great signs from heaven,' indicating clear eschatological markers rather than vague unrest.

questions.question: What doctrine regarding the faithfulness of God's word is taught in Luke 21:33?
options: God's word is subject to change depending on circumstances.
God's word is eternal and will never pass away despite the passing of heaven and earth.
God's word is only valid during the lifetime of Jesus.
Heaven and earth will never pass away.
questions.correctAnswer: God's word is eternal and will never pass away despite the passing of heaven and earth.
questions.explanation: Luke 21:33 clearly states 'Heaven and earth shall pass away: but my words shall not pass away,' affirming the eternal truth and faithfulness of God's word.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated by God's judgment described in Luke 21:22?
questions.correctAnswer: Wrath
questions.explanation: Luke 21:22 refers to 'these be the days of vengeance,' showing the attribute of divine wrath executing judgment to fulfill what is written.

questions.question: What theological synthesis can be drawn from Luke 21:3 and Luke 21:4 regarding the nature of giving in the kingdom of God?
options: Giving is only valuable if it comes from abundance.
God values sacrificial giving from poverty more than abundant giving from wealth.
The amount given is the sole measure of generosity.
Rich giving is better than poor giving.
questions.correctAnswer: God values sacrificial giving from poverty more than abundant giving from wealth.
questions.explanation: Luke 21:3-4 contrasts the rich giving from abundance with the poor widow giving 'all the living that she had,' teaching that sacrificial giving is esteemed above mere abundance.

questions.question: How does Luke 21:16 teach about the human sinfulness that results in betrayal among believers?
options: Human relationships remain unbroken despite persecution.
Sinful human nature can lead to betrayal even among close kin for the sake of opposition to Christ.
questions.correctAnswer: Sinful human nature can lead to betrayal even among close kin for the sake of opposition to Christ.
questions.explanation: Luke 21:16 states 'ye shall be betrayed both by parents, and brethren, and kinsfolks, and friends,' showing how sin affects human relationships under persecution.
